summary: Creates a binary matte by comparing selected image channel data against a threshold.

key_params.name: comparator
key_params.note: Comparison operation against the threshold; matching pixels are set to 0

key_params.name: rgb
key_params.note: Channel or aggregate used for RGB thresholding

key_params.name: threshold
key_params.note: Threshold value used by the comparator

key_params.name: alpha
key_params.note: Alpha output source, either following RGB or forcing alpha to one

key_params.name: soften
key_params.note: Falloff around the threshold for smoother mattes

common_gotchas: Official comparator semantics set pixels satisfying the comparison against Threshold to 0, which is easy to invert mentally.
Alpha can follow the threshold result or be forced to one, so RGB and transparency may not carry the same matte.
Hard thresholding creates aliased/noisy mattes; use soften or prefiltering for smoother masks.
key_concepts: Threshold TOP compares a selected image channel or aggregate against a threshold to generate binary image regions.
The comparator defines which pixels are forced to 0, while the remaining pixels form the nonzero side of the matte.
RGB thresholding and alpha output are controlled separately, allowing opaque RGB masks or alpha-following masks.
The soften control creates a transition band around the threshold for smoother keyed edges.
